name: Central Bank (Individual Accountability Framework) Act 2023 + SEAR Regulations
reference: Act No. 5 of 2023 + CBI SEAR Regulations + Conduct Standards Regulations + F&P Regulations

articles.title: Duty of Responsibility (reasonable-steps)
articles.section: IAF Act s.20A inserting CBR Act 2010 s.21H
articles.requirement: Where a regulated financial service provider commits a prescribed contravention, a person performing a PCF role allocated responsibility for the relevant matter is liable unless they prove they took such reasonable steps as a person in their position could be expected to take to avoid the contravention. Reverse burden — PCF holder must adduce evidence of reasonable steps.

articles.title: Conduct Standards — power to make
articles.section: IAF Act Part IIA (CBR Act 2010 amendments)
articles.requirement: The CBI is empowered to prescribe Conduct Standards for individuals performing Controlled Functions in regulated financial service providers. Standards include Common Conduct Standards (all CFs) and Additional Conduct Standards (PCFs).

articles.title: Administrative Sanctions Procedure (ASP) extended to individuals
articles.requirement: Individuals may be sanctioned directly under the ASP without the prior requirement to establish the firm's contravention as a 'participation link'. Penalties up to €1 million for individuals; disqualification, prohibition + censure also available. F&P investigations may run in parallel.

articles.title: PCF identification + allocation
articles.requirement: The firm must identify each PCF role applicable to it (from the CBI's PCF list), the individual holding that role, and ensure the appointment has CBI pre-approval. PCF-1 Executive Director, PCF-3 Chair, PCF-8 CEO, PCF-11 CFO, PCF-12 Head of Compliance, PCF-14 Head of Risk, PCF-15 MLRO, PCF-2B (I)NED (added 1 Jul 2025), and 50+ others depending on firm type.

articles.title: Management Responsibilities Map (MRM)
articles.requirement: The firm maintains a single document — the Management Responsibilities Map — setting out: (a) each PCF role + holder; (b) reporting lines; (c) Inherent Responsibilities; (d) Prescribed Responsibilities + their allocation; (e) Other (firm-specific) Responsibilities + their allocation; (f) board + committee structure; (g) material delegations. Kept current; produced to CBI on request.

articles.title: Statement of Responsibilities (SoR)
articles.requirement: For each PCF the firm prepares a Statement of Responsibilities setting out: (a) the individual's allocated responsibilities (Inherent + Prescribed + Other); (b) reporting line; (c) scope of role + business / control areas. Signed by the individual + acknowledged by the firm. Updated on material change; submitted to CBI within prescribed timeframes (new appointment, change of responsibilities, departure).

articles.title: Inherent Responsibilities
articles.requirement: Responsibilities inherently attaching to each PCF role per CBI Guidance. Examples: Chair (PCF-3) — leading the board's effectiveness; CEO (PCF-8) — implementation of board strategy + operational performance; CFO (PCF-11) — integrity of financial information + financial controls; Head of Compliance (PCF-12) — compliance framework. Inherent Responsibilities cannot be reallocated.

articles.title: Prescribed Responsibilities
articles.requirement: Specific responsibilities prescribed by CBI that must be allocated to one or more PCF holders. Includes: PR1 risk-management framework; PR2 ICAAP + capital adequacy; PR3 ILAAP + liquidity adequacy; PR4 financial-crime systems + controls; PR5 ICT / cyber resilience; PR6 regulatory reporting integrity; PR7 business continuity + operational resilience; PR8 whistleblowing; PR9 conduct + culture; PR10 outsourcing + third-party risk; further PRs depending on firm type.

articles.title: Other (Firm-Specific) Responsibilities
articles.requirement: Material business + control responsibilities specific to the firm beyond Inherent + Prescribed — allocated by the firm to PCF holders in the MRM. Captures the long tail of accountability (specific product lines, geographies, business units, regulatory programmes).

articles.title: (I)NED scope expansion (1 July 2025)
articles.requirement: From 1 July 2025 (I)NEDs are within SEAR scope as PCF-2B. They are subject to the Common Conduct Standards and (where their role makes them senior management) the Additional Conduct Standards, F&P pre-approval, and require Statements of Responsibilities reflecting their specific board / committee role allocations (chair of a committee, senior independent director, etc.). Every in-scope firm had to refresh its MRM + onboard (I)NED SoRs by this date.

articles.title: Common Conduct Standards (CCS)
articles.requirement: Five standards applying to every individual performing a Controlled Function in a regulated financial service provider: (1) act with honesty + integrity; (2) act with due skill, care + diligence; (3) cooperate with the CBI + relevant regulators in an open + cooperative way; (4) act in customers' best interests + treat them fairly + professionally; (5) operate compliance with the standards of market conduct.

articles.title: Additional Conduct Standards (ACS)
articles.requirement: Four additional standards applying to PCFs (and certain CFs with senior management responsibility): (1) take reasonable steps to ensure that the business of the firm for which you are responsible is controlled effectively; (2) take reasonable steps to ensure the business of the firm for which you are responsible complies with relevant regulatory requirements; (3) take reasonable steps to ensure that any delegation of your responsibility is to an appropriate person + you oversee the discharge of the delegated responsibility effectively; (4) disclose appropriately any information of which the CBI would reasonably expect notice.

articles.title: F&P pre-approval (PCFs)
articles.requirement: An individual may not perform a PCF role without prior CBI approval. The firm submits an Individual Questionnaire + supporting documents covering competence, experience, integrity, financial soundness. CBI may approve, refuse, or attach conditions. Appointment without approval is a regulatory breach.

articles.title: F&P ongoing certification (CFs + PCFs)
articles.requirement: The firm is required to satisfy itself on an ongoing basis (at minimum annually) that each PCF + CF holder remains fit + proper. Material changes (criminal proceedings, bankruptcy, regulatory action elsewhere) must be considered + (where appropriate) reported to CBI. Annual certification by the firm; records retained.

articles.title: F&P investigation + sanction powers
articles.section: IAF Act amendments to CBR Act 2010
articles.requirement: CBI may investigate an individual's fitness + probity; suspend the person from CF performance during investigation; issue prohibition notices (temporary or permanent). The IAF Act 2023 substantially widened these powers, including for non-CF persons exercising significant influence.

articles.title: Breach reporting under SEAR + F&P
articles.requirement: Firms must report to the CBI: (a) any disciplinary action taken against a PCF / CF for breach of Conduct Standards within prescribed timeframes; (b) issues that may affect a person's fitness + probity (criminal, civil, regulatory); (c) the departure of a PCF + the reasons. Standalone of the wider general reporting obligations to CBI.

articles.title: Handover Procedures (transitions)
articles.section: SEAR Regs Pt IV(4) + CBI Guidance
articles.requirement: On a PCF transition the outgoing + incoming individuals must support a documented handover. CBI Guidance expects: a handover certificate or note covering material risks, ongoing investigations, open regulatory matters, pending board decisions, key relationships. The MRM + SoRs are updated; the new SoR filed with CBI as soon as practicable.
